title: Odessa jazz party founded by Dr. Fulcher
summary: Leeman is hired again for Gibson's 1979 party, his 17th, then explains how Dr. Jim Fulcher founded the invitation-only Odessa, Texas jazz party.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: I'm going to attempt to do a couple of like -- I have to skipover so much and not get deeply into the subject, but I want to get into the subject of some of the jazz parties that are spin offs from the Gibson parties, and I'm gonna start, as Milt Hinton will agree with me, I'm sure -- the next big one for us was the Odessa jazz party. So I'll get into that one now.

My thoughts were just interrupted here -- a telephone call from Dick Gibson, from Denver, and he just hired me again, for his 1979 jazz party at the Broadmore Hotel in Colorado Springs this coming Labor Day weekend, and this will be my 17th year. I consider that a pretty good average!
Now for the Odessa party. For the past two years, we've missed the original ingredient for the Odessa party. I'll go on to explain.

The Odessa party was a dream of a gentleman, Dr. O.A. Jim Fulcher, who was an eminent surgeon and a lover of jazz music. After visiting Gibson's parties as a guest, he got together with a few influential citizens in Odessa, Texas, and they formed a committee called the Odessa Jazz Unlimited Incorporation.
They backed the first concerts there. Their first parties were also private parties -- it was a guest list, invitation only -- and they still are. Their list is sold out,
and it's growing every year. This'll be my 13th year there this May.
